title: Cocartesian fibrations are Joyal categorical fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and the horn definitions of cartesian and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], extended over arbitrary simplicial bases as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. In a fixed universe let $p:X\to S$ be either a cartesian fibration or a cocartesian fibration of simplicial sets. Then $p$ is a fibration in the Joyal model structure. Explicitly, for every degreewise injective categorical equivalence $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and maps $f:A\to X$ and $g:B\to S$ with $pf=gi$, there is a simplicial map $h:B\to X$ satisfying $hi=f$ and $ph=g$. No quasicategory or nonemptiness assumption on $X,S,A,B$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, printed pp. 209-210; the cocartesian assertion is its opposite.
source.note: Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Start with a lifting square over the arbitrary base $S$, where $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is a degreewise injective categorical equivalence. Factor the terminal map of $S$ in the Joyal model structure as a categorical equivalence $j:S\to T$ followed by a Joyal fibration $T\to\Delta^0$. Since the terminal simplicial set is a quasicategory, the fibrancy clause of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $T$ a quasicategory. The factorization is in the input universe, and no hypothesis on $S$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, proof, first sentence (factor $S\to\Delta^0$ through an infinity category)

proof.text: Work first with a cartesian fibration $p$. The family of relative marked model structures required as hypotheses by [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance] is supplied by [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]: the weak equivalences, fibrant objects, sharp mapping enrichment, base-change Quillen adjunctions and universe-relative factorizations are precisely those stipulated there. Its tensor is $U\times K^\sharp$ by the defining sharp mapping adjunction. Apply clause (2) of the base-equivalence statement to $j:S\to T$ and $p:X\to S$. Obtain a cartesian fibration $q:Y\to T$ and a cartesian-edge-preserving map $u:X\to Z=S\times_TY$ over $S$, whose pullback along every map to $S$ is a categorical equivalence. By the base-change clause of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], $Z\to S$ is cartesian and its natural marking is the pulled-back natural marking of $Y$.

For each vertex $s:\Delta^0	o S$, the universal comparison of [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance] gives a categorical equivalence $u_s:X_s	o Z_s$. Thus the fiber criterion of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] makes $u:X^
atural	o Z^
atural$ a weak equivalence between fibrant marked objects over $S$. Its inverse criterion supplies a marked map $v:Z^
atural	o X^
atural$ over $S$ and a path $\eta$ from $vu$ to $\operatorname{id}_X$ in $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(X^
atural,X^
atural)$. This is an actual path over $S$, not a homotopy claimed to be constant on $A$. If given as an edge path, combine consecutive edges by $2$-horn fillers in this Kan complex and reverse edges by $2$-horn fillers with a degenerate edge, obtaining a single edge with the indicated endpoints.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, proof, the maps $u,v$ and their homotopies over $S$

proof.text: Let $a=\operatorname{pr}_Yuf:A\to Y$. Since $T$ is a quasicategory, [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] says that $q:Y\to T$ is a Joyal fibration. The square with top $a$, bottom $jg:B\to T$ and left side $i$ commutes, since $qa=jpf=jgi$. Apply its right lifting property from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] to obtain $k:B\to Y$ with $ki=a$ and $qk=jg$ strictly. Therefore $w=(g,k):B\to Z$ is defined and $wi=uf$, because both coordinates agree. Set $r=vw:B\to X$. Then $pr=g$ and $ri=vuf$. This performs the source's extension and base correction in one strict lift, using only the already established quasicategory-base case.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, proof, extension into $Y$ and correction over $T$; combined by the quasicategory-base lifting clause

proof.text:
Regard $A^ lat$ as an object over $S$ via $gi=pf$ and $B^ lat$ via $g$. The map $f:A^ lat	o X^
atural$ preserves markings because only degenerate edges of $A$ are marked. Precompose the path $\eta$ of step 3 with $f	imes\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^1}$ to obtain an edge $\eta_f$ from $vuf=ri$ to $f$ in $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(A^ lat,X^
atural)$. By [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], restriction $R:\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(B^ lat,X^
atural)	o\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(A^ lat,X^
atural)$ is a Kan fibration, since $i$ is a monomorphism and $p$ is cartesian over the arbitrary base $S$. Apply its horn lifting property for $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ to the vertex $r$ and the edge $\eta_f$. The endpoint is a marked map $h:B^ lat	o X^
atural$ over $S$ with $R(h)=f$. On underlying simplicial sets this says $ph=g$ and $hi=f$ strictly. This supplies the diagonal without presupposing that $p$ is a Joyal fibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, proof, final relative homotopy correction; its extension justified by Lemma 3.1.3.6

proof.text: For a cocartesian $p$, reversal of the order on each simplex turns $p$ into the cartesian fibration $p^{\mathrm{op}}$, by the opposite horn convention of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. It preserves monomorphisms degreewise. It also preserves categorical equivalences as defined in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]: for every quasicategory $C$, reversal identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},C)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(B,C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and identifies their homotopy categories with the corresponding opposite categories; $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory because reversal sends inner horns to inner horns. Thus restriction along $i^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an equivalence by the test for $i$ against $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and passage to opposite ordinary categories. Reverse the given square, apply the cartesian case to obtain $h^{\mathrm{op}}$, and reverse again. The two strict triangle identities become $hi=f$ and $ph=g$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, opposite dual; self-duality noted immediately after its proof

proof_origin.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7, printed p. 209; expanded using the quasicategory-base lifting clause and Lemma 3.1.3.6 for the final homotopy extension

This serves the coherent adjunction used in proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint; six steps give base replacement, marked inverse, strict lift, relative correction and opposite dual.

split_report.summary: Six-step arbitrary-base lifting proof following HTT Proposition 3.3.1.7: replace the base, extend the cartesian fibration, obtain a marked inverse from its vertex fibers, solve the square strictly over the quasicategory base, and correct the restriction using the Kan fibration on relative sharp mapping complexes. Dualize with the explicit categorical-equivalence test on opposites. Independent second reading repaired unsupported homotopy assertions; no new nodes.

I checked the statement against HTT Prop. 3.3.1.7 from memory; it is that proposition plus its cocartesian dual, not weakened. I checked each proof step against the cited node statements. Step 1: the Joyal factorization makes T a quasicategory. Step 2: every hypothesis of base-equivalence-invariance (2) is supplied by marked-relative-cartesian-model, including the tensor U×K♯ from the enrichment; the base-change clause gives the natural marking on Z. Step 3: the vertex fibers give a weak equivalence between fibrant objects, hence v and a path vu~id. Step 4: q is a Joyal fibration over T, and qa=jgi, w=(g,k), wi=uf, pr=g, ri=vuf all hold strictly. Step 5: restriction of sharp mapping complexes along i is a Kan fibration over an arbitrary S; lifting at r gives hi=f and ph=g. Step 6: the opposite argument is correct and elementary enough. Small cases checked: point base, empty A (forces B empty), empty S or X, identity fibration. No new nodes, no duplicate in the DAG, no cycle, all citations in the same unit, no tool_uses, no SGA. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem cocartesian_joyal_fibration {X S : SSet.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (_hp : Marked.Over.relativeFibration false p ∨ Enhanced.cocartesianFibrationOver p) (A B : SSet.{u}) (i : A ⟶ B) (_hi : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (i.app n)) (_he : ∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), Quasicategory C → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map i)).app C)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) (f : A ⟶ X) (g : B ⟶ S) (_comm : f ≫ p = i ≫ g) : ∃ h : B ⟶ X, i ≫ h = f ∧ h ≫ p = g
